Jennie fills an aquarium, in the shape of a rectangular prism that is $50\,\text{cm}$ long and $25\,\text{cm}$ wide, with water from a tap. How fast is the volume of water in the aquarium changing if the water level is rising at a rate of $0.2\,\text{cm}/\text{h}?$

The volume of water in the aquarium is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
${\text{cm}}^{3}\text{/h}.$
question.worked_solution:
We define the following variables:

- let $L$ and $W$ be the length and width of the aquarium, respectively, and

- let $h$ and $V$ be the height and volume of the water, respectively.

Note that $h$ and $V$ change with time, while $L$ and $W$ are constants. 

We are given that

$$
L=50\,\text{m},\,W=25\,\text{m},\,\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}=0.2\,\text{m}/\text{min}.
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}.$

The relation between the two time-dependent variables, $V$ and $h,$ is given by the formula for the volume of water:

$$
V=LWh
$$

We differentiate both sides of $V=LWh$ with respect to $t,$ treating both $L$ and $W$ as constants, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}V & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(LWh) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =LW\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can plug in the known values and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =(50)(25)\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =1250\cdot 0.2 \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =250.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of water in the aquarium is increasing at a rate of $250\,{\text{cm}}^{3}\text{/h}.$
